bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and a preserved ejection fraction, spironolactone vs placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.04).
implications: These data support that spironolactone did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome versus placebo (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.04; P = 0.14). They do support a lower incidence of hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.99; P = 0.04), while also showing higher hyperkalemia (18.7% vs. 9.1%) and increased serum creatinine levels, with no significant reduction in death from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.08; P = 0.29) or hospitalization for any reason (hazard ratio, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.85 to 1.04; P = 0.25).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in HFpEF comparing spironolactone vs placebo.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned 3445 patients with symptomatic heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45% or more to receive either spironolactone (15 to 45 mg daily) or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of CV death, aborted cardiac arrest, or HF hospitalization.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, aborted cardiac arrest, or hospitalization for the management of heart failure.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was not significantly reduced with spironolactone.
major_points.quote: the primary outcome occurred in 320 of 1722 patients in the spironolactone group (18.6%) and 351 of 1723 patients in the placebo group (20.4%) (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.04; P = 0.14).

major_points.text: Hospitalization for heart failure was significantly lower with spironolactone.
major_points.quote: only hospitalization for heart failure had a significantly lower incidence in the spironolactone group than in the placebo group (206 patients [12.0%] vs. 245 patients [14.2%]; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.99, P = 0.04).

major_points.text: Hyperkalemia was higher with spironolactone (about doubled).
major_points.quote: Treatment with spir­on­olactone was associated with increased serum creatinine levels and a doubling of the rate of hyperkalemia (18.7%, vs. 9.1% in the placebo group) but reduced hypo­kalemia.

major_points.text: Neither death from any cause nor hospitalization for any reason differed significantly between groups.
major_points.quote: Neither total deaths nor hospitalizations for any reason were significantly reduced by spironolactone.
